text: its much better now. still could use some love. just wondering, wouldnt it be a better approach if the user interface had 0 delay, and everything just resolves its whole scene graph behind the scenes. i see something like 'confirming...' in the top corner but its never putting me in any delayed state
resolution: Built the optimistic-UI flow the user specified (00c20d9ab): release costs zero, the scene resolves behind the scenes, an amber 'confirming…' pill (top-left of the iso pane) is the only sign anything is still landing. Mechanism: the drag ghost is already mounted with stable keys, so on mouse-up it simply turns SOLID with its real skins/edits — it IS the building — while the originals hide from the instanced standing render and the store batch defers one tick (setTimeout 0). When the standing pieces reflect the change, the overlay drops — confirm is a prop swap, never a remount, so there is no blink and no frozen release. Covers move (solid ghost at destination + originals hidden), wall-line/floor-rect paint (cells stay rendered solid), tower (ground ring holds while the full shell lands), and delete (selection vanishes this frame). Validation still runs synchronously BEFORE anything optimistic so a refused edit never shows a phantom; any pieces change (undo, co-session) clears overlays while the deferred batch still applies — eventually consistent. Bundle clean; heavy verify deferred per the no-builds-during-live-session protocol. Try: drag a wall line or move the building — it should stand the instant you let go, with only the pill blinking.
